candidate.blueprint_locator: Client Needs category 'Psychosocial Integrity' — nursing care that promotes emotional, mental and social well-being; applied here to coping, self-concept, therapeutic communication and social/professional support.
candidate.educational_objective: Respond therapeutically to cancer-related guilt and self-blame by assessing its effect on coping and relationships, avoiding reinforcement of blame, and facilitating appropriate emotional and social support.

options.A: Acknowledge the guilt without reinforcing self-blame, explore how it is affecting coping and relationships, and offer counseling or support resources if the feelings are difficult to manage.
options.B: Tell the client that guilt is useful because self-blame is necessary to prevent cancer from recurring.
options.C: Avoid discussing the guilt because emotional reactions after cancer treatment have little relevance to survivorship care.
options.D: Explain that withdrawing from friends is the healthiest way to manage guilt until the feeling disappears on its own.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NCI states that many people with cancer experience guilt and may blame themselves for lifestyle choices they believe contributed to cancer. NCI advises that having cancer is not the person's fault and recommends sharing feelings with trusted people, counselors, support groups, or the healthcare team. NCI also recognizes guilt/self-blame and avoidance of people as possible cancer-related post-traumatic stress symptoms, so persistent or disruptive distress warrants assessment and support. B reinforces unsupported causal blame and incorrectly links guilt with recurrence prevention. C dismisses a recognized psychosocial need. D promotes isolation even though NCI identifies social and professional support as potential coping resources.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NCI recognizes cancer-related guilt and self-blame, advises against blaming oneself for cancer, supports expression of feelings and counseling/support-group resources, and identifies guilt/self-blame and social avoidance among possible cancer-related stress symptoms.
candidate.source_document_title: Emotions and Cancer; Cancer-Related Post-Traumatic Stress (PDQ®)
candidate.source_locator: Emotions and Cancer — heading 'Guilt' and 'More Ways to Cope with Your Emotions' → 'Express your feelings' and 'Don't blame yourself for your cancer'; Cancer-Related Post-Traumatic Stress PDQ — symptom list including guilt/self-blame and avoiding people, plus treatment section supporting counseling and support groups.
candidate.source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
candidate.stem: A cancer survivor tells the nurse, 'I keep blaming myself for choices I made before I got cancer. I feel so guilty that I have stopped talking to my friends about what I am going through.' Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?
